text_blocks.snippet: Therapy for dogs with anxiety can involve behavior modification techniques, calming aids, and, in some cases, medication. Desensitization and counterconditioning are common training methods to help dogs become less fearful of specific triggers. Calming aids like pheromone diffusers, pressure wraps, and interactive toys can also provide relief during stressful situations. In more severe cases, veterinary behaviorists may recommend medication to help manage anxiety.
snippet_highlighted_words: behavior modification techniques, calming aids, and, in some cases, medication

list.title: Desensitization and Counterconditioning:
list.snippet: These techniques are used to gradually expose a dog to the source of their anxiety at a low intensity, while simultaneously teaching them a positive behavior to replace the anxious response. For example, if a dog is afraid of thunderstorms, they might be gradually exposed to recorded thunderstorm sounds at a low volume while being rewarded with treats for remaining calm.
